articles.title: Un écran gamer QHD 180Hz à moins de 140€ : la bonne affaire Lenovo du moment
articles.text:
Boulanger fait chuter le prix de l'écran PC gamer Lenovo LOQ 27Q-10, un moniteur QHD 180 Hz pensé pour les joueurs qui cherchent la fluidité sans exploser leur budget. À 139,99 €, cette référence mérite qu'on s'y attarde d'un peu plus près.
Voici le Lenovo LOQ 27Q-10 à 139,99 € au lieu de 159,99 € chez Boulanger !
Lenovo poursuit l'expansion de sa gamme LOQ, initialement pensée pour les configurations gaming accessibles, avec cette fois un écran dédié. Le LOQ 27Q-10 mise sur une diagonale de 27 pouces et une définition QHD (2560 x 1440 pixels) pour offrir un bon compromis entre confort visuel et charge graphique raisonnable.
On peut actuellement se procurer ce moniteur via cette offre Boulanger, à un tarif qui le positionne clairement sur le segment de l'entrée de gamme performante. Ce bon plan s'adresse en priorité aux joueurs qui montent une configuration avec un budget écran limité, sans vouloir sacrifier la fluidité. Reste à savoir si les caractéristiques techniques de ce modèle tiennent la comparaison face aux standards actuels du marché gaming.
Pourquoi choisir le Lenovo LOQ 27Q-10 ?
- Fluidité maximale : le taux de rafraîchissement de 180 Hz associé à un temps de réponse de 0,5 ms (MPRT) limite les flous de mouvement lors des phases de jeu rapides.
- Confort visuel en QHD : la définition 2560 x 1440 pixels et la certification HDR10 offrent une image plus détaillée qu'un écran Full HD classique, sans nécessiter une carte graphique surpuissante.
- Connectique tournée vers le gaming récent : deux ports HDMI 2.1 et un DisplayPort permettent de brancher aussi bien un PC qu'une console de dernière génération.
Un moniteur pensé pour les sessions de jeu prolongées
Ce Lenovo LOQ 27Q-10 embarque la technologie Adaptive-Sync, compatible AMD FreeSync, qui synchronise le taux de rafraîchissement de l'écran avec celui de la carte graphique pour limiter les déchirures d'image. Les modes de filtrage de la lumière bleue et anti-scintillement, présents ici, participent au confort lors de longues sessions devant l'écran. Dans son comparatif des meilleurs écrans PC gamer, la rédaction de Clubic rappelle qu'un taux de rafraîchissement compris entre 138 et 180 Hz représente aujourd'hui la norme pour un usage gaming polyvalent, ce qui correspond exactement au positionnement de ce modèle Lenovo. Le pied ajustable en hauteur et l'inclinaison réglable permettent par ailleurs d'adapter la position de l'écran à sa morphologie, un point souvent négligé sur les moniteurs d'entrée de gamme.
Face à la concurrence, un positionnement clairement tarifaire
Sur le segment des écrans QHD 180 Hz, plusieurs références se positionnent au-delà de 200 euros, notamment celles proposant une dalle OLED ou un taux de rafraîchissement supérieur à 240 Hz. Le LOQ 27Q-10 ne rivalise pas avec ces modèles plus premium, mais il coche les cases essentielles pour un premier écran gamer QHD à un tarif nettement plus accessible.
✅ Les points forts
- Taux de rafraîchissement de 180 Hz et temps de réponse de 0,5 ms pour une fluidité réelle en jeu
- Définition QHD associée à la certification HDR10 pour une image détaillée
- Deux ports HDMI 2.1, compatibles avec les consoles récentes
- Technologie Adaptive-Sync (AMD FreeSync) pour limiter le tearing
- Pied ajustable en hauteur et inclinable, câble DisplayPort fourni
❌ Les limites
- Écran non pivotable en mode portrait
- Absence de revêtement anti-reflets
- Haut-parleurs intégrés non confirmés par le fabricant
- Luminosité de 300 cd/m² en retrait face aux modèles plus premium
Le Lenovo LOQ 27Q-10 reste actuellement affiché à 139,99 € chez Boulanger, sous réserve des stocks disponibles.
Le Lenovo LOQ 27Q-10 remplit son rôle d'écran gamer d'entrée de gamme performant. À 139,99 euros, il propose une définition QHD, un taux de rafraîchissement de 180 Hz et un temps de réponse de 0,5 ms, soit des caractéristiques rarement réunies à ce tarif. Cette offre s'adresse en priorité aux joueurs qui montent ou complètent une configuration avec un budget écran limité, sans vouloir se contenter d'une dalle Full HD classique.
Les amateurs de dalles OLED, de luminosité élevée ou de taux de rafraîchissement supérieur à 240 Hz devront en revanche se tourner vers des références plus onéreuses. Pour un usage gaming polyvalent sans prétention haut de gamme, ce moniteur Lenovo constitue une option cohérente à surveiller pendant que le prix reste appliqué.

articles.title: Google's AI told people Flock cameras were full of gold. They weren't.
articles.text:
Facepalm: For a short while, Google's AI Overviews handed the internet a financial case for vandalizing Flock's AI-powered license plate cameras, and it wasn't based on anything real. Google has since walked the answer back, but the incident is a clean example of how quickly a widely used AI tool can turn a joke into something that looks like fact.
The story starts with a meme: privacy advocates joking online that Flock's surveillance cameras are secretly loaded with valuable metals, worth cracking open for scrap. AI Overviews took the joke literally, and for a while, told anyone who asked exactly that.
Until recently, anyone searching "how much gold does a Flock camera have" saw a confident answer: a "Flock safety camera contains about 1 to 5 grams of gold used in its internal circuit boards and wiring," plus between two and 23 pounds of copper.
Taken literally, that put roughly $650 worth of gold, and an implausible amount of copper, inside a device that weighs just three pounds. The figures didn't match what engineers would expect from this kind of compact electronics, and of course weren't backed by teardown data or materials analysis.
Image credit: Futurism
After the discrepancy was reported, Google appears to have updated the answer. The AI answer now pushes back directly, telling searchers that claims of a single unit holding pounds of recoverable copper are false since the whole housing weighs about three pounds, and that any gold present is only in trace amounts typical of small consumer electronics.
Some users saw this new language, too: "A Flock safety camera only contains trace amounts of gold in its standard electronic circuit boards, similar to most common small electronics. Rumors claiming the cameras are packed with large amounts of valuable precious metals – like ounces or grams of recoverable gold – come from internet memes and AI hallucinations, not facts."
Flock's cameras sit at the center of a growing AI surveillance network. The units use cameras and machine learning models to capture license plate images, translate them into machine-readable text, and feed that data into searchable databases used by police and private customers.
The process is automated end to end: the system scans passing vehicles, runs the plates through recognition software, and surfaces hits in seconds. Those capabilities – continuous data capture, AI-based identification, and fast search across large datasets – have made Flock a focal point in debates over how far automated monitoring should go, especially as reports emerge of officers using the system for unauthorized checks on romantic partners.
The technology has also become a lightning rod because it reflects where modern security tools are headed: networked cameras, automated recognition, and large, queryable datasets about everyday movement.
Online, the backlash has spawned an ecosystem of memes and videos celebrating the destruction or sabotage of the cameras. One recurring joke casts Flock's units as high-tech piñatas, packed with gold, copper, and other metals rich enough to make vandalism pay. The premise is simple: cut down the hardware, crack it open, strip out the "valuable" components, and cash in at the scrapyard.
The underlying economics don't hold up. Like most electronics, the cameras contain small amounts of precious and base metals in their boards, connectors, and wiring, but the quantities are tiny, and extracting them takes time, tools, and know-how.
Without experience breaking down circuit boards, the realistic payoff is closer to pocket change than a serious cash haul. The meme glosses over that reality.
Google's earlier AI Overview answer lent the meme a veneer of credibility, repeating it almost verbatim and backing it with two weak sources. The first was an anonymous Substack post from an account called do.not.obey.do.not.comply, claiming the "rough scrap value of these metals per camera is estimated to be $150 to $500."
The post itself admitted the figures came from "estimates based on scrap-value discussions," not testing, teardown documentation, or formal analysis.
The second was an AI-generated Instagram post urging people to rip apart Flock cameras for scrap. The account mostly posts about growing weed, plant cloning, and hydroponics, with no apparent expertise in hardware engineering.
For people using AI systems, the episode is a reminder of how easily a summarization tool can turn casual speculation into what looks like a technical statement. The model scans available content, finds material that fits the question, and stitches it into a clean, confident-sounding answer.
In this case, nothing suggests it checked whether the numbers made sense for a three-pound device, or weighed the credibility of anonymous and AI-generated sources. The output sounded certain even though the underlying data was flimsy.
The episode also exposes how prone AI models still are at missing context. The scrap-value narrative around Flock is part humor, part protest against AI-driven surveillance, exaggerating the hardware's value to make a point about the cameras themselves. Google's system didn't get the joke. It treated the posts as straightforward claims and repeated them as facts.

articles.title: Lavadora vs. lavadora secadora: qué diferencias hay y cuál te conviene elegir según fabricantes
articles.text:
La elección entre una lavadora y una lavadora secadora se ha convertido en una decisión clave para quienes buscan eficiencia, ahorro de espacio y un mejor manejo de la ropa en casa. Los fabricantes destacan diferencias fundamentales en consumo energético, capacidad, tiempo de uso y funcionalidad que pueden influir en la elección del electrodoméstico más adecuado según cada necesidad.
Este tema importa hoy porque, en un contexto de hogares más pequeños y tarifas energéticas en constante cambio, la optimización del consumo y la comodidad marcan la pauta en las tendencias de electrodomésticos. Entender cómo funcionan y qué ventajas ofrece cada opción permite tomar una decisión informada y evitar gastos innecesarios a largo plazo.
PUBLICIDAD
¿Qué diferencias hay entre una lavadora y una lavadora secadora?
Una lavadora tradicional está diseñada exclusivamente para el lavado de prendas. Su ciclo suele tardar alrededor de una hora y, según fabricantes como Kalley, LG y Samsung, el consumo energético depende del tipo de ciclo seleccionado y la frecuencia de uso. En cambio, la lavadora secadora integra en un solo equipo la función de lavado y secado, permitiendo realizar ambos procesos de manera consecutiva y sin necesidad de manipular la ropa entre ciclos.
La principal ventaja de la lavadora secadora es la comodidad: se puede lavar y secar la ropa en un solo paso, ideal para espacios reducidos o para quienes buscan simplificar tareas domésticas. No obstante, esta funcionalidad adicional implica ciertas diferencias relevantes en consumo y duración de los ciclos.
PUBLICIDAD
Consumo energético: ¿qué gasta más?
Los fabricantes coinciden en que, si se utiliza únicamente la función de lavado, el gasto de una lavadora secadora es similar al de una lavadora convencional. El aumento significativo ocurre cuando se emplea el ciclo completo de lavado y secado, ya que el proceso de secado requiere más potencia y tiempo.
Por ejemplo, una lavadora secadora típica puede utilizar una resistencia de 1200W para el secado, lo que puede extender el ciclo total hasta seis horas dependiendo de la cantidad de ropa y la configuración elegida. El ciclo de secado es el que más energía consume, ya que implica generar calor durante un periodo prolongado. En comparación, una lavadora tradicional puede completar su ciclo en cerca de una hora y con un consumo energético más acotado.
PUBLICIDAD
Capacidad y eficiencia
Otro aspecto relevante es la capacidad de carga. Los modelos de lavadora secadora suelen tener una capacidad de secado menor que la de lavado, por lo que no siempre es posible secar toda la carga en un solo ciclo. Esto puede obligar a dividir la ropa en tandas, lo que repercute tanto en el tiempo como en el consumo energético.
La eficiencia también varía según el modelo y la tecnología incorporada. Algunas marcas han implementado sistemas de bajo consumo, sensores de humedad y programas inteligentes para optimizar el gasto energético y minimizar el impacto ambiental.
PUBLICIDAD
Ventajas de cada opción
Lavadora:
- Menor consumo energético si solo se requiere lavado.
- Ciclos más cortos y mayor capacidad de carga en modelos estándar.
- Menor costo inicial y mantenimiento más sencillo.
Lavadora secadora:
- Comodidad de lavar y secar en un solo equipo, ideal para espacios pequeños.
- Solución práctica para quienes no pueden tender ropa al aire libre o en climas húmedos.
- Ahorro de tiempo y esfuerzo en la manipulación de prendas entre ciclos.
Qué conviene elegir según el uso y el espacio
La elección depende de varios factores: el tamaño del hogar, la frecuencia de lavado, el clima local y el presupuesto disponible. Para quienes lavan grandes volúmenes de ropa o buscan minimizar el gasto energético, la lavadora tradicional sigue siendo la opción más eficiente. En cambio, la lavadora secadora es la mejor alternativa para departamentos pequeños, climas lluviosos o rutinas con poco tiempo.
PUBLICIDAD
Consejos para optimizar el uso y ahorrar energía
- Seleccionar programas eco o de bajo consumo en ambos equipos.
- No sobrecargar la lavadora ni la secadora para garantizar un desempeño eficiente.
- Aprovechar las horas valle de tarifa eléctrica, si están disponibles.
- Mantener el equipo limpio y realizar el mantenimiento indicado por el fabricante.
Elegir el electrodoméstico adecuado, según las recomendaciones de los fabricantes y las necesidades del usuario, permite optimizar recursos, ahorrar energía y facilitar las tareas del hogar.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: iPhone 18 Pro could be in short supply soon after launch: report
articles.text:
Supply of the iPhone 18 Pro may be constrained at launch due to wider component shortages.
According to Culpium, a lack of DRAM could make it harder to get the Apple handset, which is expected to be unveiled in September. While the publication notes that production of Apple’s A20 Pro processor is “progressing well,” there’s a backlog on the DRAM side. In total, the site reports that about US$1 billion worth of Apple processors are sitting around waiting for DRAM before the next phase of production can begin.
Culpium says Apple and its manufacturing partners are “confident that they can meet initial demand” but have concerns that post-launch inventory will quickly deplete.
What could make this issue worse is the fact that Apple is reportedly not planning to introduce a base iPhone 18 model this year. Instead, the company is expected to only debut the higher-end iPhone 18 models and its long-rumoured foldable iPhone Ultra during its usual September keynote. The base iPhone 18 and lower-cost Air 2, meanwhile, are said to be slated for 2027. Therefore, your only options for new iPhones this year will very likely be the (more expensive) iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max and iPhone Ultra.
At any rate, we won’t have to wait long to find out. The company is expected to hold this year’s fall iPhone event either on Wednesday, September 8 or Thursday, September 9, right after the Labour Day holiday. We should find out an exact date and time soon.
Source: Culpium

articles.title: Organ donation group accused of trying to take living man's organs faces shutdown
articles.text:
The US health department is working to shut down a Kentucky-based organ procurement organization that made headlines over a 2021 incident in which it was accused of trying to harvest a man’s organs while he was still alive.
In an announcement Wednesday, the Department of Health and Human Services said it had begun the process to decertify the organization, Network for Hope (NFH). Losing its certification would effectively shutter the organization, which serves Kentucky as well as parts of Indiana, Ohio, and West Virginia. If decertified, another organization will be appointed to coordinate donations in the region.
In a statement, NFH said it “strongly disagrees” with the HHS’s finding and will appeal the decertification decision.
HHS said its decision stems from two federal investigations of NFH that found “persistent patient safety failures,” despite extensive oversight and opportunities to correct failures. The two investigations were carried out separately by the HHS’s Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services and the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA).
The HRSA investigation, which concluded last year, examined 351 NFH cases in which organ donations had been authorized but were ultimately canceled. In 103 cases, investigators found “concerning features,” including 73 cases in which patients had neurological signs that should have made them ineligible for organ donation.
The scrutiny over NFH and other organ procurement organizations comes amid increases in donations from people who have had circulatory deaths (their heart stops), rather than those who have been declared brain-dead. Donation after circulatory death often occurs when patients are not expected to make a recovery and a family decides to withdraw life support. Organ procurement organizations cannot declare a person dead and are barred by law from being involved in care decisions. However, deciding when to remove life support is not clear-cut.

The US launch introduces pricing and availability from American hardware retailers, giving US-based users access to localized offers rather than converted European prices.
PC Hardware Price Comparison for US Builders
Shopping for PC hardware often requires checking several retailers, comparing product variants, and determining whether an apparent discount is actually a good deal. DropReference brings offers from multiple retailers together on a single product page. articles.title: OpenAI says it stopped an Asian scam campaign hijacking ChatGPT to lure in victims
articles.text:
OpenAI says it stopped an Asian scam campaign hijacking ChatGPT to lure in victims
Multiple ChatGPT accounts were banned
- OpenAI disrupted a major scam campaign in Cambodia’s Poipet, banning accounts and blocking new registrations
- Criminals used ChatGPT to run romance fraud, fake investments, bogus police scams, and even operations linked to human trafficking
- AI was leveraged for fake personas, fraudulent messages, job lures, and worker administration; OpenAI shared findings with authorities after evidence of hundreds of victims losing thousands of dollars
OpenAI said it disrupted a major scam campaign coming out of Southeast Asia by banning accounts used by the operation and making it difficult to open new ones.
In a blog post, the ChatGPT maker said it was tipped off about the existence of the campaign by WhatsApp.
After investigating further, the company found that a group of criminals in Cambodia used its AI tool in different scam campaigns - romance fraud, fake investment scams, or bogus police investigations. It also used AI to help with day-to-day operations and, most worryingly, for things that could be related to human trafficking and forced criminality.
Detention and escape attempts
OpenAI did not say if the group had a name, just that it operated out of Poipet, “a city in Banteay Meanchey province that public reporting has repeatedly linked to online scam compounds and trafficking operations.”
The group used AI to create fake personas, to help draft fraudulent emails and chat messages, and to create posters for fake jobs which were probably used to lure people into human trafficking or forced labor.
The tool was also used for worker administration, since the operators maintained records of employee debts, salary deductions, disciplinary fines, and loan repayments. They also used the tool to translate discussions about immigration status, work permits, visa overstays, and recruitment incentives.
“Some conversations also referenced apparent detention, escape attempts, and potential criminal liability for people who had been trafficked and forced to work in scam operations,” OpenAI said. “While these conversations do not allow us to determine the circumstances of any particular individual, they are consistent with extensive public reporting describing the activities of organized crime groups in Southeast Asia.”

articles.title: Xovian is building satellites that listen for radio signals rather than take images
articles.text:
Xovian is building satellites that listen for radio signals rather than take images
The Bengaluru-based company is developing radio-frequency nanosatellites with onboard processing, aimed at tracking ships and aircraft that optical imaging cannot.
An imaging satellite needs daylight and a clear sky. Cloud, darkness or a vessel that simply moves between passes will defeat it. Radio frequency sensing works differently: it detects the signals a ship, an aircraft or their radar emits, which travel regardless of weather or light, and reveal something a photograph cannot, namely what a piece of equipment is doing.
was founded in 2019 by Ankit Bhateja and Raghav Sharma, and works out of Bengaluru. Its stated aim is a constellation of radio frequency nanosatellites, small spacecraft that capture and interpret signals rather than images. Its investors have described the team as having built satellites and space-grade components before, with cost and scalability as the design constraint.
The specific gap the company points to is a familiar one in maritime monitoring. Ships are required to broadcast their position, and a vessel that wants to avoid being tracked turns that transponder off. It goes dark to optical and transponder-based systems alike, but it does not stop emitting other signals.
Processing in orbit rather than on the ground
What the company calls AI-native is the design decision underneath the constellation. A conventional satellite collects data and sends it down for analysis, which can introduce delays ranging from minutes to hours, depending on the system. Xovian's stated approach is to interpret the signals aboard the spacecraft, so what reaches the ground is already an insight rather than a raw feed.
That matters for the applications it names. Tracking a vessel that has gone dark, or an aircraft, or a pattern of radar activity, is only useful while the information is current. The company describes low-latency, high-fidelity output as the point of the architecture.
The hardware ambition is a multi-frequency radio frequency sensor developed in India. At the time of its pre-seed round, the company said the payload would fly aboard an ISRO launch vehicle to validate the sensing technology, with space trials expected by the end of 2025.
It positions the result as sovereign radio frequency intelligence, meaning capability India owns rather than buys. Its named markets run across government, enterprise and humanitarian users, and it has talked about pilots in India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
Nanosatellites are what make the economics work. A constellation needs many spacecraft to revisit the same patch of ocean often enough to be useful, and small satellites are cheap enough to launch in numbers.
Two rounds, and a satellite still to fly
Xovian raised $2.5 million in a pre-seed round announced in August 2025, led by Piper Serica and Turbostart with Inflection Point Ventures and Eaglewings Ventures participating. In April 2026, it raised a further $2 million, about Rs 18.7 crore, in a round led by the investor Ashish Kacholia, with Inflection Point Ventures returning.
The second round is for developing the first radio frequency satellite, expanding the engineering and AI teams, and building commercial partnerships. Total disclosed funding across both rounds stands at about $4.5 million.
The company sits in a sector filling quickly. Pixxel, SatSure and Dhruva Space are all working on satellite data from India, though on optical imaging and analytics rather than radio frequency, and Xovian's positioning rests on that being a different problem.
The space trials described as expected by the end of 2025 have not been announced. The company's own description of the April 2026 round, which is for developing its first satellite, suggests the payload has yet to fly.
(This story has been researched and compiled using publicly available information.)

articles.title: Cyber resilience emerges as downtime hits $19M per hour - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cyber resilience emerges as a distinct investment category as downtime costs hit $19M per hour
Cyber resilience is no longer considered a mere technical concern, but a board-level business imperative and a direct investment category. In terms of recovery speed, the organizations that treat it as such will bounce back faster when disruption hits.
That evolution is well underway, according to Christy Wyatt (pictured), president and chief executive officer at Absolute Security. New research published by the company at Black Hat 2026 found that the average cost of one hour of endpoint downtime across 1,000 CISOs surveyed is $19 million. However, despite growing awareness of the problem, only 4% of those same practitioners said they felt genuinely ready to recover from a major disruption.
“I think the first is the cost of one hour of downtime. If we took across the — we had 1,000 CISOs participate in the survey — $19 million an hour. That’s a crazy number,” Wyatt said. “$19 million an hour is what the average was across that community. If we want to talk about how do we minimize downtime, we can put a dollar amount on it.”
Wyatt spoke with Krista Case at Black Hat USA during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how cyber resilience is emerging as a distinct market category, why the CISO’s role is expanding to encompass recovery in addition to prevention and what separates organizations that recover quickly from those that don’t. (* Disclosure below.)
Cyber resilience demands rehearsal, board involvement and endpoint recovery infrastructure
Most organizations run tabletop exercises that stop at the point of containment. They know how to identify and remediate a threat, but they have never played the scenario all the way through to the question of how to get 5,000 downed devices back online while the business is still trying to operate. Minimum viable operations, communication protocols and device recovery workflows are the steps that get skipped, and of course, they’re the ones that fail when a legitimate event takes place.
“Ask yourself what would happen if 60% of your endpoint devices got wiped out tomorrow morning,” Wyatt said. “Do those people know what they’re supposed to do and where they’re supposed to go and how they’re supposed to communicate with one another?”
Absolute Security’s strategy for endpoint security resilience is based on a firmware-embedded technology called Persistence, which is baked into hardware from 28 PC manufacturers and covers the majority of enterprise laptops deployed throughout the past two decades. It’s an anchor that allows the platform to reach a device regardless of its software state. It pulls forensics, restores network connectivity, or executes a remote, bare-metal reinstall without requiring the device to be physically returned to IT. The goal is to compress recovery from weeks to minutes, Wyatt noted.
“If the answer from IT was: ‘we think you clicked on ransomware, please box that laptop up and ship it back in a FedEx box,'” Wyatt said. “If we can say, actually, we’ll just pull the forensics from that device, and we’ll do a remote bare metal reinstall, and you’ll be back up and running in 25 minutes — that’s probably better.”
Boards that have reached cyber fluency now need to take the next step, Wyatt said, asking not just about risk posture but about what happens operationally when the lights go out. The CISO increasingly owns recovery as well as prevention, but the CFO, CIO, general counsel and board all have roles to play. After all, the research found that more than 72% of CISOs have already expanded their remit to include overseeing cyber resilience.
“The right conversation at the boardroom and with the senior management team is not, have you rehearsed for a cyber event?” Wyatt said. “But have you rehearsed your overall resilience? Have you written that down, practiced it, rehearsed it?”

articles.title: Bose lance le QC Headphones (Gen 2) : la marque pique le meilleur du QC Ultra, sans faire exploser la facture
articles.text:
Bose lance le QC Headphones (Gen 2) : la marque pique le meilleur du QC Ultra, sans faire exploser la facture
Fidèle à sa stratégie des petits pas, Bose fait évoluer son QC Headphones avec un design modernisé, des fonctions héritées du QC Ultra Headphones et une réduction de bruit annoncée comme plus efficace. Une mise à jour discrète, mais qui entend maintenir le casque dans la course.
Si ses produits parviennent à rester actuels et à pratiquement toujours s’imposer comme des références dans leurs catégories, Bose est connu pour ses mises à jour très discrètes, voire minimales. En effet, le QC Headphones premier du nom est quasiment identique à son aîné QC 45, qui lui-même l’était par rapport au QC 35. Le QC Headphones (2e génération) ne fait pas exception à la règle, mais force est de reconnaître une volonté d’évolution sans faire grimper la facture.
Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2e génération)
Ce nouveau casque Bluetooth de milieu/haut de gamme entend donc moderniser le design de son emblématique prédécesseur tout en héritant de fonctionnalités jusqu’alors réservées au QC Ultra Headphones (2e génération) , le fleuron du catalogue de Bose.
Une esthétique moderne empruntée au QC Ultra
Côté design, la principale nouveauté réside dans l’abandon du système de réglage cranté un peu daté, au profit d’un ajustement interne coulissant, plus discret. Il est ainsi possible de déployer le casque sans que cela n’altère son esthétique, tandis que cette évolution a permis d’affiner les branches dans un souci d’épure. On note également un rembourrage recouvert de similicuir plus étendu que sur la première génération, à l’image du QC Ultra, tandis que Bose annonce avoir retravaillé la force de serrage afin de trouver le meilleur compromis entre confort et maintien.
Parmi les autres détails, on note des boutons physiques mieux intégrés ainsi qu’un tissu acoustique désormais coloré, tandis que son poids demeure contenu à 230 g, ce qui en fait toujours l’un des casques sans fil les plus légers du marché.
Technologie True Spatial et audio lossless en USB-C
Bien qu’il y en ait toujours avec la marque américaine, comme c’était le cas lors des lancements des QC Ultra Earbuds (2e génération) et du QC Ultra Headphones (2e génération), Bose ne donne aucun détail sur d’éventuelles optimisations acoustiques, si ce n’est la reconduction de son traitement numérique du signal SoundDesign. Héritant de la technologie True Spatial déjà présente sur le modèle Ultra, le QC Headphones (2e génération) met l’accent sur l’audio spatial, qui applique une spatialisation tridimensionnelle à n’importe quelle piste audio. Celle-ci se décline en trois modes : Still, Motion et Cinema, proposant respectivement une scène sonore fixe, un suivi des mouvements de tête et une virtualisation optimisée pour les contenus audiovisuels.
À l’instar de son grand frère, le QC Headphones (2e génération) introduit aussi la prise en charge des flux audio sans perte jusqu’à 24 bits/48 kHz à partir de n’importe quelle source via son port USB-C. En contrepartie, le casque abandonne le port mini-jack 3,5 mm de son aîné, mais est tout de même livré avec un câble mini-jack vers USB-C pour une connexion aux sources analogiques.
Intoduction d'ActiveSense, ANC mieux adpaté aux fuites acoustiques, etc.
Comme sur les autres modèles, l’audio spatial Immersion peut être activé directement via les commandes du casque, tout comme le mode Cinema, le mode Conscient et la réduction de bruit baptisée Silencieux. Ce dernier aurait d’ailleurs été amélioré par rapport à celui du QC Headphones, notamment grâce à une meilleure adaptabilité aux fuites acoustiques, afin de conserver un bon niveau d’isolation lorsque l’on porte des lunettes ou si le casque vient à légèrement se déplacer.
Par ailleurs, Bose annonce une meilleure efficacité de la technologie ActiveSense associée au mode Conscient, qui applique temporairement la réduction de bruit lorsqu’un bruit soudain est détecté. De plus, comme sur le QC Ultra Headphones (2e génération), il est désormais possible de désactiver entièrement ces traitements afin d’utiliser le casque en isolation passive.
L’application propose également accès à un égaliseur 3 bandes toujours aussi chiche, à la gestion des appareils Bluetooth appairés, à la personnalisation partielle des commandes, entre autres. Enfin, la marque promet des appels plus clairs en environnement bruyant grâce à un algorithme annoncé comme plus efficace.
Connectivité toujours chiche, autonomie inchangée
Côté connectivité, si le casque passe à une puce Bluetooth 5.4 moderne, Bose n’a communiqué ni sur une éventuelle compatibilité avec des codecs avancés ni sur la prise en charge de la norme LE Audio. Il est donc probable que le QC Headphones (2e génération) se contente des codecs AAC et SBC, l’aptX Adaptive demeurant l’apanage du QC Ultra. En revanche, le multipoint et Google Fast Pair sont toujours de la partie afin de permettre une connexion simultanée à deux appareils et un appairage simplifié sur Android.
Le QC Headphones (2e génération) promet une autonomie de 24 h, comme son prédécesseur, tandis qu’une fonction de charge rapide permettrait de récupérer jusqu’à 2 h 30 min d’écoute après seulement 15 min de charge.
Le casque est disponible en précommande dès aujourd’hui pour les membres My Bose, et les premières expéditions sont prévues pour le 13 août. Il est proposé au tarif de 349,95 € dans des coloris inédits hérités du QC Ultra (Eucalyptus Green, Menthe Rosée et Mauve Rosé), en plus des classiques noir et blanc.
Bien qu’il soit affiché 50 € moins cher que le QC Headphones à son lancement, conformément à la nouvelle stratégie tarifaire du constructeur américain, son prix paraît particulièrement élevé pour un casque historiquement positionné à mi-chemin entre le milieu et le haut de gamme. À l’heure où le Sennheiser Momentum 4 Wireless est toujours disponible sous la barre des 200 € et où le Nothing Headphone (1) a franchi un nouveau cap en matière de rapport qualité/prix, ce nouveau venu devra convaincre autrement que par son seul nom. Rappelons toutefois que le QC Headphones (2e génération) a vocation à voir son prix diminuer au fil du temps, comme en témoigne la première génération, désormais commercialisée en dessous de 250 €.

articles.title: Toda a memória prevista para 2027 já esgotou (e a culpa é da IA) • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Toda a memória prevista para 2027 já esgotou (e a culpa é da IA)
Impulsionada pelo boom da inteligência artificial, a produção de gigantes como Samsung e Micron atingiu o limite, ameaçando a oferta e encarecendo componentes para PCs e celulares.
Se você estava planejando montar um PC ou comprar um smartphone, é bom preparar o bolso. As três maiores fabricantes globais de semicondutores (Samsung, SK Hynix e Micron) já venderam toda a capacidade de produção de memórias projetada para 2027.
O principal fator por trás do esgotamento de estoques entre julho e agosto de 2026 foi a corrida desenfreada por infraestrutura de inteligência artificial.
A resposta está na mudança de foco do mercado. O avanço acelerado da IA exige data centers que dependem de memória. Essa necessidade fez com que a demanda superasse a capacidade total de fabricação em uma escala inédita.
Para não atrasar projetos, grandes empresas optaram por trabalhar com exclusividade no fornecimento, por medo de ficar sem componentes. Com isso, o mercado de chips estabeleceu um modelo de negócios favorável aos fornecedores, que agora podem ditar as regras e os preços.
Com quase toda a produção disponível comprometida, o mercado de dispositivos para o usuário final vai sofrer. O presidente da fabricante de hardware ADATA, Chen Li-bai, projeta que as aplicações focadas em IA vão devorar cerca de 70% da capacidade de produção de memória RAM.
Isso significa que a fatia que sobra para abastecer notebooks, computadores de mesa e smartphones será muito menor em 2027. Atualmente, os fabricantes de eletrônicos de consumo conseguem comprar apenas 60% a 70% das metas originais ou dependem de sobras dos fornecedores.
A alta nos preços de peças e aparelhos é um efeito cascata natural. Chey Tae-won, presidente do Grupo SK, estima que a demanda total por chips de memória crescerá entre 50% e 60% em 2027. A busca específica por chips voltados para IA pode dar um salto de até 100% em relação aos números de 2026.
O impacto dessa matemática já aparece em projeções do mercado. A estimativa é que o preço da memória RAM suba mais 40% globalmente. No Brasil, empresários do setor confirmam que o preço da memória já aumentou 30%.
Analistas projetam que a escalada de preços vista ao longo de 2026 vai perder força em 2027, já que a maior parte da produção foi alocada agora. No entanto, o valor já estará fixado no topo. Como a Lenovo já havia alertado ao mercado, a alta nos preços das memórias veio para ficar. A nova norma da indústria é a pressão de custo, que refletirá no bolso do consumidor final.

articles.title: Explosive drone found hovering near Ukrainian cargo aircraft at German airport
articles.text:
German police disarmed a drone carrying explosives after it was discovered near Ukrainian cargo aircraft parked at Leipzig airport—and authorities are looking into the possibility of a second drone after an approaching aircraft collided with something midair.
The drone was first spotted by an airport employee hovering close to the ground between two parked An-124 cargo aircraft owned by Ukraine’s Antonov Airlines shortly before midnight on August 4, according to The Guardian. It had apparently been modified to help avoid detection by the airport’s drone defense sensors, said Alexander Dobrindt, federal minister of the interior for Germany, during a press conference.
Dobrindt described the drone as carrying a fist-sized package of a substance believed to be the plastic explosive Semtex. Only a failed detonator prevented the drone from exploding near the Ukrainian cargo aircraft, he said.
German police used a bomb disposal robot to help disarm the drone and later carried out a controlled explosion, according to BBC News.
Contrary to some media reports, the German Interior Ministry has denied that the apparently targeted Ukrainian cargo aircraft were carrying weapons or other munitions for delivery to Ukraine, according to Deutsche Welle. Instead, government officials described the aircraft as having been empty at the time of the drone incident.
The incident forced Leipzig/Halle airport—one of Europe’s largest air cargo hubs—to close to all air traffic for several hours. That forced 19 flights to divert away from the airport, including a Boeing 757 operated by the shipping company DHL that was forced to abort its landing approach, according to the flight tracking service Flightradar24.
As the DHL-operated aircraft started climbing again, it collided with another flying object midair and diverted to land at Hanover airport with minor damage, German police reported in a statement. German authorities are looking into the possibility that the object was a second drone.
The possible culprit and motive
German officials have not officially named a suspect behind the attempted attack, but have opened a counterterrorism investigation. Dobrindt acknowledged that “we are dealing with a contest here that possibly involves foreign powers,” and described the incident as a “hybrid threat scenario.”

articles.title: Vikra Ocean Tech builds underwater robots for inspection, survey and defence work
articles.text:
Vikra Ocean Tech builds underwater robots for inspection, survey and defence work
The Chennai-based company makes remotely operated vehicles, autonomous surface vessels and crawling robots, along with the cameras and lighting that go on them.
India has a long coastline, a great many dams and reservoirs, and a growing need to inspect what sits under the water in all of them. The machines that do that work, remotely operated vehicles and the cameras and lights they carry, have almost all been imported. That makes them expensive, slow to service, and designed for conditions that are not Indian
was founded in Chennai in 2019 by Rajeuv Govindan and Rajagurunathan Krishnasamy to build them indigenously instead. The company describes its aim as an indigenous ocean robotics stack, covering both what goes under the water and what floats on it, and says its systems are designed for Indian operating conditions.
The word stack matters to how the company positions itself. Rather than assembling imported parts, it says it builds the components too: cameras, lighting, diver communication systems and AI-based video enhancement, alongside the vehicles themselves.
Underwater and over it
The product range covers four things. Deep-water remotely operated vehicles (ROVs) do subsea inspection and intervention work. Autonomous surface vessels float over the water for survey missions. Amphibious crawling robots move across the seabed. Imaging and communication systems tie the rest together.
All of it runs through a single control platform, which is the company's argument for interoperability: an operator can run different machines from the same interface rather than learning four separate systems.
The hardware claim it repeats most is depth. Vikra says its deep-ocean camera and lighting systems are rated to 2,000 metres, which is well below where sunlight reaches and where pressure becomes the main engineering constraint. It says its autonomous surface vessels are being used in offshore marine exploration.
The applications it names run across defence, subsea infrastructure inspection, hydrographic survey and disaster response. Its own website adds dam, bridge and reservoir inspection, aquaculture and environmental research, which is the commercial side of the same technology.
India has a large number of ageing dams and bridges whose underwater structures need periodic inspection, work that is currently done by divers or by imported equipment. That is the civilian market a defence-capable machine can also address.
A million dollars, and two grants
The company raised $1 million, about Rs 8.8 crore, in a seed round announced in April 2026 and co-led by Finvolve and India Accelerator. The money is for scaling manufacturing, building a sales pipeline across defence and public sector undertakings, and setting up recurring revenue through service and maintenance contracts.
Before that, it had won two grants under the Ministry of Defence's Innovations for Defence Excellence programme, one from the Indian Army and one from the Indian Coast Guard. These are equity-free awards for developing a capability a service has asked for, and they are a signal that a customer has taken an interest, not that an order has followed.
Finvolve and India Accelerator have described subsea robotics as becoming a strategic priority for India across defence, infrastructure and disaster response, which is the case the round was made on. Both have backed several early hardware companies working on import substitution.
What is not public is the commercial record. No customer, contract value, delivered unit count or revenue figure appears anywhere, and the shift from grant-funded development to recurring service revenue is the thing this round is meant to fund rather than something already achieved.

articles.title: -70% sur le Lefant M210 : un robot aspirateur à moins de 90€ chez Amazon
articles.text:
L'été s'annonce chargé entre les départs en vacances et l'envie de retrouver un intérieur propre au retour. Le robot aspirateur connecté Lefant M210 profite d'une remise de 70 % chez Amazon, de quoi automatiser l'entretien des sols sans y consacrer le moindre week-end.
Le Lefant M210 s'adresse à ceux qui veulent déléguer une tâche répétitive sans investir dans un modèle haut de gamme. Ce robot compact mise sur la simplicité : trois modes d'aspiration, une programmation via l'application Lefant et une compatibilité avec Alexa pour un pilotage vocal. Actuellement affiché à 89,95 € au lieu de 299,99 €, cette offre repérée chez Amazon vise particulièrement les foyers avec animaux et les petites surfaces.
Pour les propriétaires de chats ou de chiens qui redoutent les poils incrustés dans les fibres du tapis, ce format d'entrée de gamme peut constituer un point de départ pertinent avant de partir en congés. Il ne remplace pas un grand ménage de printemps, mais il évite que la poussière ne s'accumule pendant une semaine d'absence, ce qui change concrètement l'ambiance d'un logement au retour de vacances.
Voici le Lefant M210 à 89,95 € au lieu de 299,99 € chez Amazon !
Pourquoi choisir le Lefant M210 ?
- Prix cassé : 89,95 € au lieu de 299,99 €, soit une remise de 70 % chez Amazon.
- Format compact : environ 28 cm de diamètre pour moins de 8 cm de hauteur, capable de se glisser sous la plupart des meubles bas.
- Pilotage simplifié : application Lefant, programmation des cycles de nettoyage et compatibilité Alexa pour un usage sans contrainte.
Un robot pensé pour l'entretien courant, pas pour remplacer un aspirateur principal
Le Lefant M210 se concentre sur l'essentiel : aspirer poussière et poils sur sols durs et tapis fins, sans fonction de lavage ni cartographie avancée. Sa buse sans brosse centrale limite les enchevêtrements, un point appréciable pour les foyers avec un chat ou un chien à poils mi longs. Dans son test consacré à ce modèle, la rédaction Clubic l'a essayé pendant plusieurs jours et confirme qu'il reste efficace sur les poils d'animaux, même si sa navigation par capteurs de proximité reste plus basique qu'un système laser. Ce positionnement en fait avant tout un robot d'appoint, utile en complément d'un ménage occasionnel plutôt qu'en remplacement complet d'un aspirateur traditionnel.
L'application Lefant permet de programmer des créneaux de nettoyage à l'avance, ce qui prend tout son sens pour qui souhaite que le robot passe pendant une absence prolongée. Le retour automatique à la station de charge en fin de cycle évite également d'avoir à surveiller l'appareil, un argument qui pèse pour un usage estival sans supervision quotidienne.
Face aux modèles plus avancés, un choix d'entrée de gamme assumé
Comparé aux robots dotés de LiDAR, d'une station de vidage automatique ou d'une fonction lavante, le Lefant M210 reste en retrait sur la précision de navigation et l'autonomie de gestion au quotidien. Il compense par un prix nettement inférieur et une prise en main immédiate, sans réglage complexe à anticiper avant de partir. Dans son comparatif des aspirateurs robots, Clubic rappelle que les modèles réellement complets démarrent généralement à deux ou trois fois ce tarif, ce qui replace la promotion du M210 dans son juste contexte : un dépannage abordable, pas un concurrent des références premium.
✅ Les points forts
- Prix très attractif pour un robot connecté, à 89,95 € au lieu de 299,99 €
- Format fin qui passe sous la plupart des meubles bas
- Buse sans brosse centrale, limitant les enchevêtrements de poils
- Compatible Alexa et pilotable depuis l'application Lefant
- Retour automatique à la base de charge en fin de cycle
❌ Les limites
- Pas de cartographie laser, navigation plus approximative
- Absence de fonction de lavage des sols
- Moins adapté aux tapis épais ou aux grandes surfaces
- Bac à poussière à vider manuellement, sans station de vidage automatique
Lefant M210 à 89,95 € chez Amazon : une offre à vérifier avant votre départ en vacances !
Le Lefant M210 ne cherche pas à rivaliser avec les modèles premium et l'assume pleinement. À 89,95 €, il rend service à qui veut simplement déléguer l'aspirage quotidien avant de partir plusieurs jours, sans se soucier de la poussière qui s'accumule pendant l'absence.
Les propriétaires d'animaux et les petites surfaces y trouveront un allié pratique et accessible, capable de tenir la maison propre entre deux grands nettoyages. articles.title: Apple, Sony, and Nintendo pocketed their tariff refunds, this PC cooling company won't
articles.text:
Recap: Companies that import products into the US are still receiving an estimated $166 billion in refunds after the Supreme Court rolled back last year's historic tariffs. However, consumers bore much of the burden of the duties through higher prices, and most businesses are keeping or reinvesting the refunds. PC cooling supplier Arctic, however, is bucking the trend by lowering prices across its entire US product lineup.
Arctic has temporarily discounted its products in the US until its tariff refund is fully exhausted. The policy contrasts sharply with those of larger manufacturers that have declined to compensate customers for tariff-driven price increases.
In messages posted on YouTube and its website, Arctic explains that it absorbed the Trump administration's steep 2025 tariffs for as long as possible before passing some of the added costs on to consumers by raising prices on select products. The company, which primarily sells cooling equipment for custom PCs, has since lowered prices across its entire US catalog, not just the products affected by the tariffs.
Arctic is one of many companies owed an estimated $166 billion in combined refunds after the Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration had overstepped its authority by imposing the tariffs. Duties on some Asian countries critical to tech manufacturing exceeded 25%, while tariffs on Chinese imports climbed above 100% at times. The government has paid out roughly half of the refunds so far.
Quarterly financial reports from Sony and Apple, both of which raised prices following the tariffs, have already highlighted the impact of the refunds. Apple alone is expected to receive an estimated $2.2 billion. However, rather than passing the money on to customers, the company confirmed it will reinvest the funds in domestic manufacturing, aligning with the tariffs' original goal.
Nintendo has aggressively fought a lawsuit from customers seeking compensation, arguing that it has no legal obligation to reimburse consumers who voluntarily paid the higher prices. Sony, which is also among more than 100 companies facing similar lawsuits, has not disclosed its plans. Meanwhile, Amazon has confirmed plans to compensate customers in limited cases without providing additional details.
Beyond rolling back prices, Arctic has also pledged to invest in US-based technology education and grassroots organizations by donating hardware and providing technical support. Walmart and BJ's have likewise promised to lower prices, while Costco says it will pass its refunds on to customers, although it has not explained how.

articles.title: Canada announces $10 million investment in EV manufacturing facilities
articles.text:
The Government of Canada has announced a $10 million investment in order to build two new EV manufacturing facilities.
The investment, made through the Strategic Response Fund, will go to Hanon Systems, a company that specializes in thermal management for EVs and Hybrid vehicles, to support the construction of a manufacturing plant for vapour-injected electric compressors. Alongside this, the funding will also go towards a product development centre in Vaughan, Ontario.
The project is expected to cost Hanon Systems $198.75 million, and the plant is expected to produce up to 1.5 million e-compressors per year by 2034. The development centre in Vaughan is expected to create around 300 jobs.
Currently, Hanon Systems operates three facilities in Canada: two plants in Belleville (fluid transport) and one plant in Concord (electronics and fluid pressure), which together have a total headcount of 900 employees.
This announcement comes months after Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the new automotive strategy, which introduced a new rebate and a $1.5 billion investment in the Canada Infrastructure Bank’s Charging and Hydrogen Refuelling Infrastructure Initiative.

articles.title: Apple pide frenar la creación del dispositivo de IA de OpenAI: lo acusa de tener información filtrada
articles.text:
Apple solicitó a un tribunal detener el desarrollo de un dispositivo de inteligencia artificial diseñado por OpenAI. La petición formal, presentada en una corte según TechCrunch, asegura que un grupo de extrabajadores filtró información que llevó ante la compañía de Sam Altman.
Ante esta petición, los creadores de ChatGPT ya respondieron negando tener información de Apple para el desarrollo de su primer dispositivo con IA, pero la solitud sigue en proceso.
PUBLICIDAD
De qué acusa Apple a OpenAI por el desarrollo de su dispositivo de IA
La raíz de la demanda radica en el temor de Apple a perder el control sobre tecnologías no anunciadas y desarrollos estratégicos. La empresa sostiene que varios exempleados, entre ellos ingenieros y directivos, accedieron y, presuntamente, compartieron información reservada con OpenAI antes de dejar sus puestos.
El caso surgió inicialmente con el señalamiento directo a Chang Liu, ingeniero senior de sistemas, y Tang Yew Tan, director de hardware en Apple y luego responsable de hardware en OpenAI.
PUBLICIDAD
Según los documentos judiciales, el conflicto se agravó cuando Apple, a través de sus investigaciones internas, identificó a otros 11 extrabajadores que podrían haber tenido algún tipo de participación en el acceso o transmisión de información confidencial.
Entre ellos figura Yu-Ting Peng, quien habría sido alertada por Chang Liu sobre la intención de acceder y utilizar datos privados de la compañía.
El expediente detalla situaciones específicas: un exempleado se reunió con Liu y Peng antes de que Peng se presentara a una entrevista en OpenAI, y durante ese encuentro discutieron detalles sobre productos de Apple aún no anunciados. Además, otro extrabajador habría capturado pantallas de documentos internos vinculados a un dispositivo secreto, justo antes de asistir a su propia entrevista en OpenAI.
PUBLICIDAD
La preocupación de Apple aumentó cuando, tras la presentación de la demanda original, varios de sus antiguos empleados —ahora trabajando en OpenAI— se comunicaron para devolver equipos de trabajo que habían retenido tras salir de la empresa.
Cuál es el pedido judicial de Apple para frenar a OpenAI
El núcleo de la petición de Apple reside en la solicitud de una medida cautelar que detenga el desarrollo y lanzamiento del primer dispositivo de inteligencia artificial de OpenAI, así como cualquier otro producto que utilice tecnología presuntamente obtenida de manera ilícita.
PUBLICIDAD
En el documento presentado ante la justicia, Apple argumenta que se encuentra ante un riesgo inminente y que existe “causa fundada” para sospechar de un esquema organizado de apropiación de secretos comerciales.
La acción legal no solo involucra a OpenAI, sino también a su fundación y a la startup io, cofundada por el legendario diseñador Jony Ive, responsable del diseño del iPhone y el iPad. Apple exige un proceso de descubrimiento acelerado, es decir, una investigación judicial exprés, que permita identificar con rapidez a todos los involucrados y evitar daños irreparables a sus intereses comerciales.
PUBLICIDAD
De acuerdo con la compañía, la aprobación de la medida cautelar forzaría a OpenAI a retrasar el lanzamiento de su primer dispositivo de IA, un proyecto que ha generado expectativas en la industria tecnológica por la colaboración entre Jony Ive y Sam Altman.
La empresa sostiene que la devolución de equipos por parte de exmiembros de su equipo técnico refuerza la sospecha de que los hechos denunciados no son aislados, sino parte de un patrón más amplio de conducta.
PUBLICIDAD
OpenAI reaccionó rápidamente a la ofensiva judicial de Apple, publicando un comunicado en el que rechaza de plano las acusaciones. La empresa de inteligencia artificial califica la petición de Apple como “basada en información falsa y completamente innecesaria”, y asegura que ni posee ni tiene interés en obtener secretos comerciales de Apple.
En su declaración, OpenAI señala que su objetivo es el desarrollo de “productos y tecnologías innovadoras que empujen la frontera”, desvinculándose de cualquier supuesto interés en información ajena.
PUBLICIDAD
La controversia judicial pone en jaque el futuro del primer dispositivo de IA diseñado por Jony Ive para OpenAI. Si la corte concede la medida cautelar solicitada por Apple, el desarrollo y lanzamiento del producto quedarían suspendidos hasta que se resuelva el fondo de la demanda.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: CISO AI risk management drives business growth - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI raises the stakes for CISOs as enterprise risk decisions shift: theCUBE analysis
CISO AI risk management is emerging as the defining test of the AI era, pushing security leaders beyond blocking attacks and into the middle of enterprise decisions about how much risk a business is willing to accept. That tension is playing out this week as thousands of practitioners converge on Las Vegas, where AI has propelled the cybersecurity world into a new phase, driven by startlingly advanced autonomous attacks and an urgent need to adopt technology to defend against them.
Much of that pressure is now landing squarely on the CISO, who is increasingly expected to act as connective tissue across legal, compliance, engineering and the business itself, according to Krista Case (pictured, left), principal analyst and practice lead for cyber resilience and security at theCUBE Research.
“I’ve also been thinking about this AI governance through the lens of the different roles that the CISO has to collaborate with within the enterprise — things like legal, compliance, engineering, IT,” Case said. “They almost have to be sort of the connective tissue helping to facilitate these conversations. So they’re really becoming a business enabler.”
Case was joined by Jon Oltsik (right), analyst in residence at theCUBE Research, for a keynote analysis of Black Hat USA, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how the CISO role is evolving as AI moves from experimentation into production, alongside the invite-only summits where senior cybersecurity executives participate in candid, confidential conversation that will help to shape the next generation of cybersecurity strategy. (* Disclosure below.)
CISO AI risk management splits the market into leaders and laggards
That evolution remains far from universal. Only a narrow slice of security leaders have translated AI hype into a coherent strategy, according to Oltsik.
“About 20% of CISOs get it,” he said. “They understand the implications, they understand what their organization’s trying to do with AI. They’re looking at security architecturally. The other 80% are in a state of ignorance, sometimes ignorance is bliss, or at least assumed bliss.”
That gap in AI risk management is compounded by a disconnect between the tools flooding the show floor and the practitioners meant to evaluate them, according to Oltsik. Instead, CISOs must build threat models tied to specific business initiatives, then hand executives a clear menu of choices — accept, mitigate or transfer the risk — rather than stand in the way of adoption, he said.
“You can’t get in the way, and no one should try to get in the way — you’ll get run over,” Oltsik said. “You’ll lose your job if you try to get in the way. So that’s really the way it is.”

articles.title: NVIDIA Neural Texture Compression Now Runs on RTX Spark
articles.text:
Thursday, August 6th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
NVIDIA Neural Texture Compression Now Runs on RTX Spark
NVIDIA has officially brought its RTX Neural Texture Compression (NTC) technology to Windows-on-Arm, gearing up for a general release on its RTX Spark PC platform. First demonstrated at GTC 2026 in May, NVIDIA showcased how NTC can significantly reduce GPU VRAM usage by up to seven times. In a technology demo at one of the GTC 2026 sessions, NVIDIA revealed that NTC can lower VRAM usage from 6.5 GB to just 970 MB in certain scenes. NTC technology is an AI-driven texture output that enables games to feature high-quality, complex materials without sacrificing performance. Games can take advantage of the substantial VRAM reduction that NTC offers while maintaining the same texture quality.
For the upcoming RTX Spark, NVIDIA is enhancing the software ecosystem so gamers and future buyers receive a mature software that works seamlessly out of the box, eliminating the need for workarounds. Even Japan's legendary SEGA has released AAA titles optimized for RTX Spark and is dedicating more resources to support the ecosystem. NVIDIA has already started shipping its first preview build of the CUDA toolkit for the RTX Spark platform, specifically as a native Windows-on-Arm software toolkit. Now, emerging technologies like NTC will run on RTX Spark, which includes configurations such as one with 6,144 CUDA cores and another with 5,120 CUDA cores. Both configurations are based on the "Blackwell" GPU microarchitecture and are paired with a 20-core Arm CPU and up to 128 GB of LPDDR5X memory.Traditionally, games use block-compressed formats like BCn, such as BC5, BC6, or BC7, which are commonly applied in 4x4 pixel formats and rendered by the GPU. However, NVIDIA has trained small neural networks that can produce the desired pixel format and texture appearance at a fraction of the size of traditional texture compression formats. Instead of using gigabytes of VRAM for textures, NTC drastically reduces VRAM usage by emulating textures, allowing for either much lower VRAM consumption or significantly enhanced material appearance.

articles.title: Security's AI advantage will go to the organizations already built for accountability
articles.text:
Security's AI advantage will go to the organizations already built for accountability
Accountability infrastructure, not speed, wins enterprise AI security
The enterprise race to scale AI operations is in full swing – both from a deployment and security perspective. While conventional wisdom suggests that the teams who deploy the models first get the edge, it’s the wrong approach for enterprises.
For nefarious actors, speed is the name of the game. Malicious actors leveraging AI to probe for vulnerabilities don’t need to share their decision trail to audit committees or regulators – making speed alone the key advantage for attackers.
CEO of Edge & Node.
Enterprise security teams, on the other hand, operate under entirely different parameters – which also happen to be where the opportunity lies.
Security teams don’t just need the capability to identify anomalies, screen transactions, or make access decisions – they also need to be prepared to explain what happened, when, and why to key stakeholders.
Every action and every outcome needs to be clarified and justified to a board, an auditor, or a customer.
Scaling AI at the enterprise level is not relegated to who moves fastest, but rather who can embed the necessary accountability frameworks, emergency brakes, and audit trails.
The Hidden Data Problem
In truth, speed is not the primary challenge for most enterprise teams. The bigger, more difficult challenge is found in data and governance. Policy models and detection frameworks are only as impactful as the information inputs. However, most organizations are devoid of structured, well-governed data – particularly as it pertains to AI activity. Across the majority of organizations, data is scattered.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Activity logs, access records, transaction histories all live in disparate systems with inconsistent formats and no single source of truth. No matter how much of this data is fed into an AI model, clarity will never be achieved. Instead, teams generate a false sense of confidence built upon a shaky foundation.
Meaningful scale begins with auditability and accountability as infrastructure, not an afterthought. As AI systems become increasingly embedded across organizations, the requirement heightens for more consistent records of actions that occurred and policy enforcement where actions are checked against defined rules prior to execution.
Equally as important, organizations need to have the internal muscle memory to explain automated decisions to stakeholders outside the engineering team, because they've been doing versions of this for years in compliance and risk functions.
When this approach is foundational for enterprises, AI systems become genuinely useful. AI models built upon strong data and governance standards can meaningfully screen actions against known risks before settlement, flag patterns that humans may have missed, and maintain updated records that can be shared across key stakeholder groups. Devoid of this foundation, fragmented data and ungoverned systems compound – resulting in faster mistakes.
Enthusiasm around AI systems centers on the deployment side of the equation, without asking whether the underlying infrastructure can support what's being layered on top of it. This approach is suboptimal and leaves an open door for breaches – akin to installing an alarm system in a building without putting locks on the doors.
Embedding infrastructural policy enforcement, audit trails, and human-reviewable records does bring an additional layer prior to deployment. And in a domain where nefarious actors operate free of this operational layer, it's fair to ask whether enterprise security teams are creating a permanent speed disadvantage for themselves.
However, that mindset misses what the added operational layer actually delivers: the difference between an AI system that fails safely and one that fails silently.
Enterprise security teams who operate slower but can consistently and proactively identify and reverse bad decisions are in a fundamentally different position than enterprises who operate quickly and discover a failure three weeks post-incident. The tradeoff is real, but it’s the wrong tradeoff to optimize away.
Trust Beyond The Engineering Teams
A common misconception is that security decisions are made for and by security teams. That’s not the case. Security decisions made by automated systems need to satisfy stakeholders far outside of this workstream – including regulators, insurers, customers, even boards.
Those stakeholders aren’t moved by sophistication. They care whether the organization can clearly and consistently demonstrate what the system did and why. Organizations without that operational layer find that AI adoption increases their potential risk exposure, because they're now making faster decisions with insufficient guardrails.
As AI systems continue to increasingly exhibit autonomous behaviors, the stakes continue to change. An AI system that can initiate payments, approve transactions, or move funds independently doesn't just need a policy to follow – it needs brakes to press in the event of a bad decision.
Without this layer embedded, enterprise security teams not only carry the accountability problem – they also have no chance of catching a mistake before it becomes permanent.
The Readiness Gap
Readiness requires the proper sequencing. Before scaling AI operations, it’s critical to make an honest assessment of three things: whether underlying data across systems are structured, whether there are firm policy checks in place, and whether verifiable records of automated decisions can be produced on-demand.
Starting here positions AI to become a force multiplier for security teams. These three elements make all the difference between catching what humans miss and doing it fast enough to matter – or simply adding velocity to a faulty process.
The “AI race” will not be won by having the newest models. Really, it’s about devoting effort to the unglamorous work – building the data infrastructure and governance systems that make AI models trustworthy.

articles.title: Pre-modded 22GB RTX 2080 Ti cards surface on eBay for $500 as VRAM-hungry local AI fans chase down every spare FLOP — Hong Kong-based seller offers AI-friendly memory mod for a reasonable price
articles.text:
Pre-modded 22GB RTX 2080 Ti cards surface on eBay for $500 as VRAM-hungry local AI fans chase down every spare FLOP — Hong Kong-based seller offers AI-friendly memory mod for a reasonable price
No FLOPS left behind as the AI gold rush revives eight-year-old hardware
The AI boom means that no matrix math FLOPS are disposable, and that means older Nvidia GPUs with Tensor Cores are getting a new lease on life. Services are popping up that will outfit your RTX 2080 Ti with 22GB of VRAM, doubling its original memory pool and making it more useful for modern LLM and diffusion workloads. If you’re hard up for compute and you don't have an RTX 2080 Ti to modify, however, eBay has just the thing. A Hong Kong-based seller will send you a pre-modded 22GB 2080 Ti in exchange for $499.
The listing only promises that you'll receive a "Turbo," i.e., blower-style, RTX 2080 Ti with the 22GB mod. Don't get too picky about the particular brand of card you might receive, as the seller says: "The GPU brand could be Gigabyte, MSI, ASUS, Leadtek or others. It depends on what we have in hand."
The eBay listing photos show a Gigabyte blower-style card along with a large box of presumably modified cards ready to ship and a GPU-Z screenshot confirming the availability of 22528 MB of memory from a running card.
The seller only has 99.6% lifetime feedback on eBay, which is relatively low, but feedback for this specific listing shows that at least 38 happy buyers have received these cards and that they’re working as described.
Assuming you can count yourself as one of those happy buyers, a $500 22GB RTX 2080 Ti might be the best VRAM bang for your buck that you can find these days. That relatively large memory pool, combined with the RTX 2080 Ti's 616 GB/s of memory bandwidth and Tensor Cores, means that it's still useful for local LLM tasks, although its raw compute capacity and limited reduced-precision data type support compared to more modern products might make demanding diffusion workloads leisurely.
Among Turing cards, the 24GB Titan RTX still commands about $800 on eBay at today's prices, and a Quadro RTX 6000 with the same amount of VRAM is about $900. The local AI enthusiast's favorite RTX 3090, which has 24GB of faster GDDR6X offering 936 GB/s of memory bandwidth, looks to be selling for about $1200. Ampere RTX Pro cards with even more VRAM rapidly get more expensive from there.
The fact that all of these GPUs are still commanding such high prices many years after their introduction is a testament to the continuing utility and universal availability of Nvidia’s Tensor Core architecture across both consumer and data center products since 2018.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
AMD has had matrix math accelerators in its IP arsenal since CDNA 1 in 2020, but their availability has been limited to Instinct data center products until RDNA 4 arrived early last year. Intel included XMX matrix engines in the Alchemist architecture from the start in late 2022, but Arc graphics products have faced considerable challenges beyond the presence or absence of that capability. And Apple only just introduced Neural Accelerators to its GPUs with the M5 family.
All that means that if you’re hard up for VRAM capacity and still need a decent amount of compute to go with it, a 22GB RTX 2080 Ti could be a compelling and relatively budget-friendly way to get there, and you get access to the entirety of the CUDA software ecosystem in the bargain. Not bad for an eight-year-old GPU that might have previously ended up in the e-waste bin by now.

articles.title: Les Nuits des étoiles 2026 arrivent : où profiter du spectacle près de chez vous ?
articles.text:
Les amateurs d’astronomie vont probablement peu dormir ces prochains jours. Les Nuits des étoiles reviennent du vendredi 7 au dimanche 9 août 2026, avec des centaines de rendez-vous partout en France. Elles seront suivies, trois jours plus tard, par l’éclipse solaire du 12 août 2026. Puis, dans la nuit, par le pic des Perséides. Autrement dit, cette 36e édition donnera moins le bouquet final que le coup d’envoi.
Au total, 608 soirées d’observation sont annoncées les 7, 8, 9 et 12 août dans 415 communes. Voici comment trouver celle organisée près de chez vous.
Où observer les Nuits des étoiles 2026 ?
Pas besoin de partir au sommet d’une montagne avec un télescope dans le coffre. L’Association française d’astronomie (AFA) a mis en ligne une carte qui recense les événements organisés en France.
Chaque point correspond à une soirée et donne accès à ses informations pratiques : adresse, horaires, programme et éventuelle inscription. La carte rassemble les événements des Nuits des étoiles, mais aussi plusieurs rendez-vous prévus le 12 août pour suivre l’éclipse.
La plupart des animations sont gratuites, mais les conditions varient selon les lieux. Certaines soirées sont accessibles librement, d’autres disposent d’un nombre de places limité. Un coup d’œil à la fiche de l’événement peut donc éviter un trajet inutile.
Et si rien n’est organisé autour de chez vous, il restera toujours possible de lever les yeux depuis un jardin, un balcon ou un coin suffisamment éloigné des lampadaires. L’AFA proposera également une veillée en ligne pour guider les observations.
Et, pour la météo, faut-il s’inquiéter ?
Bonne nouvelle, la météo ne devrait pas trop perturber les observations. Vendredi soir, Météo-France prévoit un ciel clair sur la quasi-totalité du pays. Quelques nuages sont seulement attendus vers la pointe bretonne, le Cotentin et les Alpes, où de la brume pourrait aussi apparaître dans la nuit.
Samedi s’annonce encore plus favorable : le ciel devrait être dégagé presque partout en France pendant la soirée et la nuit. Un peu de pluie est néanmoins prévue autour des Pyrénées en début de soirée.
La situation sera légèrement plus incertaine dimanche soir, avec de la pluie possible vers Brest, les Pyrénées et une partie du centre du pays. Le ciel devrait toutefois se dégager dans la nuit sur la plupart de ces zones, à l’exception du Pays basque. Ces prévisions, que nous avons consultées le 3 août, peuvent encore évoluer d’ici aux Nuits des étoiles.
Que pourra-t-on observer dans le ciel ce week-end ?
Les Perséides seront déjà au rendez-vous. Cette célèbre pluie d’étoiles filantes n’atteindra son maximum que dans la nuit du 12 au 13 août, mais quelques météores pourront déjà être aperçus pendant les Nuits des étoiles.
Les télescopes permettront surtout d’explorer le ciel profond. L’Association française d’astronomie annonce qu’il sera possible de parcourir la Voie lactée du nord au sud, depuis Cassiopée et Persée jusqu’au Scorpion et au Sagittaire, en direction du centre de notre galaxie. Selon les instruments et les conditions d’observation, les visiteurs pourront également découvrir des nébuleuses, des amas d’étoiles et des galaxies.
Cette année, le thème des Nuits des étoiles sera pourtant… le Soleil. Un choix assez logique à quelques jours de l’éclipse du 12 août, durant laquelle plus de 90 % de son disque sera caché partout en France métropolitaine.
Ces trois soirées serviront donc aussi à préparer cet événement et à apprendre à l’observer sans risque. Pour rappel, même presque entièrement masqué, le Soleil ne doit jamais être regardé directement sans lunettes certifiées pour les éclipses. Des lunettes de soleil ordinaires ne suffisent pas : pensez donc à vous équiper de lunettes certifiées.
L’éclipse solaire totale du 12 août 2026 : l’événement astronomique de la décennie
Observer une éclipse solaire est un événement rare, que l’on n’oublie pas. Surtout quand c’est une éclipse totale. La probabilité est d’en voir une est faible : une occultation totale du Soleil par la Lune ne survient que tous les 400 ans au même endroit sur la Terre.
La prochaine éclipse solaire est donc une véritable aubaine. Elle a lieu le mercredi 12 août 2026, et l’Europe est aux premières loges pour l’admirer. En Espagne ou en Islande, le phénomène s’annonce splendide : la bande de totalité de l’éclipse passe sur ces pays. Cela vaut donc le coup de songer à organiser vos vacances sur la trajectoire de l’éclipse.
En France métropolitaine, l’éclipse du 12 août sera toujours partielle, mais pas moins belle. Le Soleil sera occulté jusqu’à 99 % en fonction des lieux d’observation.
Lunettes d’éclipse solaire : le guide complet de Numerama pour ne pas se tromper
Pour profiter d’un tel phénomène astronomique, il est indispensable de s’équiper. Il ne faut JAMAIS regarder le Soleil sans protection adaptée. Des lunettes d’éclipse aux normes sont requises pour observer le Soleil disparaître derrière la Lune.
Attention à ne pas vous tromper lors de l’achat, car des lunettes d’éclipse non conformes sont disponibles à la vente en France, comme l’a constaté l’Association Française d’Astronomie (AFA) : utiliser de tels équipements représente un risque réel pour vos yeux.
